To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HPV+ / normal cytology women had lower re-test rates, especially women aged 65+, women without previous Pap, and women with self-collected samples.
HPV + / normal cytology women are less likely to attend re-test and that women with clinician collected samples are more likely to be re-tested than self collected samples.

HPV+ and normal cervical cytology women have a lower re-test rate, and that women with no record of previous cervical cancer screening, women 64+ and women who were HPV tested using clinician-collected sample had lower odds of being retested.

the implementation of HPV screening and its effectiveness, and the need to improve the quality and effectiveness of the screening programs in LMICs.
the implementation of HPV-based cervical cancer screening in a low-middle income setting.
the identification of those factors associated with the low adherence to re-test among HPV+/Cytological normal women in a low-income country.
